title: ThirdEyeProtocol

ClosedBy.description: How a clip stopped recording. Drives a badge on the clip row.

ClipStatus.description: Phone-local lifecycle of a clip. The vest never sees this.

SessionState.description: Vest capture state machine, see spec 7.6.

ConnectionState.description: Phone-local view of the control channel.

UmpireEnd.description: Which end the vest is standing at. One vest in v1; the field exists so a second unit needs no protocol change.

MarkEdge.description: Which edge of a delivery a marker represents. The umpire marks the start and the end from the app; the vest cuts the clip out of its rolling buffer afterwards.

PinReason.description: Why a clip is exempt from auto-purge. Free-text is not allowed: pin reasons end up in an audit log and must be enumerable.

ClipMeta.description: The sidecar the vest writes next to every clip, and the payload of GET /api/clips.

v.description: Protocol version this object was written by.

match_id.description: Opaque match identifier minted by the vest. Contains no personal data.

camera_id.description: Stable id of the vest unit. Present from v1 so a second unit is additive.

seq.description: Monotonic delivery counter. Wides and no-balls get their own seq.

started_at.description: Unix seconds, vest clock, including pre-roll.

preroll_s.description: Seconds of ring buffer prepended before the START press.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex of the review-copy file. The phone must verify this before committing.

over.description: Nullable: the vest does not know the score. The phone fills it in.

legal.description: False for a wide or a no-ball.

HealthSnapshot.description: Vest telemetry. Deliberately carries no video and no identifiers beyond camera_id.

encoder_fps.description: Measured, not configured. A silent drop here is the worst failure mode in the system.

buffer_held_s.description: How many seconds of footage are currently recoverable from the rolling buffer. A marker older than this can no longer be cut, which is the one thing the phone needs to know before promising the umpire a clip.

protocol.description: Highest protocol version the vest speaks. The phone refuses to pair on a major mismatch.

ring_size.description: How many clips the vest holds. The phone mirrors this rather than hardcoding 12.

buffer_seconds.description: Depth of the rolling capture buffer. Anything within this window can still be cut, which is what makes a marker queued during a Wi-Fi outage recoverable.

t.description: Echo of the client ping timestamp, for RTT.

vest_time.description: The vest's own clock at the moment it replied. With the round trip from `t`, the phone estimates the offset between the two clocks and stamps every marker in vest time - so the vest never has to track a per-client offset of its own.

MarkMessage.description:
The umpire marked the start or the end of a delivery. Replaces the BLE remote: the control now lives in the app, next to the footage.

A marker is not a trigger. The vest records continuously, so this only says which part of the buffer to keep. That is what lets a marker queued during a Wi-Fi outage still produce a clip once the link returns - the footage was never conditional on the message arriving.

seq.description: Delivery number. Minted by the phone, which is now the thing that counts deliveries.

at.description: Unix seconds in the VEST's clock, already offset-corrected by the phone. See `vest_time` on the pong message.

queued.description: True when this marker was held on the phone during an outage and is being replayed. The vest treats it identically; the flag exists so a late clip can be explained rather than looking like a fault.

since_seq.description: Highest seq the phone has committed. The vest replays everything after it that is still held.

ServerMessage.description: Vest to phone. Unknown types are ignored, never an error, so either side upgrades independently.

PairingPayload.description: The contents of the QR code on the vest. Scanned once per season, not per match.

password.description: WPA2 passphrase for the vest AP. Secret: never logged, never rendered, never synced.

psk.description: Optional 32-byte hex shared secret. When present the phone HMACs every request so another phone on the same AP cannot pull clips. See docs/THREAT_MODEL.md.
